items.title: Live: US, Iran exchange fire as Trump issues new threats and blockade begins
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he will not charge a 20 per cent toll on traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, just hours before the US Navy's blockade is set to resume.

items.title: Australia's best-paid CEO makes 500 times the average salary
items.description: Australia's most highly paid executive collected a salary nearly 500 times that of the country's full-time average worker.

items.title: University of Melbourne defends management of antisemitism on campus
items.description: A royal commission has heard the University of Melbourne has been improving its processes for students to make complaints in the wake of antisemitic experiences by staff and students which escalated in 2024.

items.title: Live: Government to force data centres to minimise water usage, underwrite own power under new AI standards
items.description: The PM is is outlining a national framework to deal with the emergence of artificial intelligence. Follow live.

items.title: Moira Deeming makes last-ditch plea to Liberal Party to retain candidacy
items.description: Victorian MP Moira Deeming faces being disendorsed as a Liberal candidate for refusing to apologise to former party leader Matthew Guy, after accusing him of assaulting her at a community event in May.

items.title: Disgraced footballer Nicky Winmar removed from AFL Hall of Fame
items.description: Winmar was found guilty earlier this month of three counts of unlawful assault and common law assault.

items.title: Man shot dead in Sydney's north-west in 'very brazen attack'
items.description: A man has been shot dead in Sydney's north-west, with the homicide squad now leading the investigation.

items.title: Sydney childcare abuse investigation expands to South Australia
items.description: A federal police investigation into an alleged childcare abuser has expanded to a remote Indigenous community in South Australia.

items.title: Timor-Leste scam centre compounds uncovered as police make 300 arrests
items.description: Police in Timor-Leste uncover a major international scam centre in the country, arresting more than 300 Chinese, Indonesian and Cambodian nationals in raids across the capital, Dili.

items.title: Woman with alleged links to Islamic State needs medical help, court told
items.description: A woman who was arrested over alleged links to the Islamic State terror group upon her arrival in Sydney has been denied bail for a second time, despite her lawyer saying she needed treatment for "significant psychological damage".

items.title: Boy, 5, dies after being hit by 4WD in suburban Perth
items.description: A five-year-old boy dies and a 48-year-old woman is critically injured after being struck by a four-wheel drive outside a park in Cloverdale in Perth's south-east,

items.title: Quick hits: Spain's secret to success, Yamal's streak and Balogun's confession
items.description: Spain showcases its biggest advantage over France, Lamine Yamal's hot streak goes on and Folarin Balogun opens up on his overturned red card. Here are today's quick hits.

items.title: Father of murdered carer wins workplace injury claim
items.description: Tony Ticehurst has won his workplace compensation case against Peabody Energy, with the judge noting his murdered daughter Molly was helping care for him before her death.

items.title: Truck driver's sacking for $100k ice cream bungle was fair, finds commission
items.description: The Fair Work Commission rules a trucking company was within its rights to fire a driver after he set the temperature of his trailer full of ice cream more than 20 degrees too warm.

items.title: The bittersweet reality of becoming an empty-nester
items.description: Experts say there can be unexpected grief for parents that comes from children leaving home.

items.title: Monet, Renoir, van Gogh masterpieces appear in two new blockbuster exhibitions
items.description: More than 150 years after the first Impressionist exhibition in Paris, the Art Gallery of South Australia and Geelong Gallery cast new light on the influential art movement.

items.title: Quiz: Dust off your passport and join us on a trip
items.description: Which of these peaks isn't in the Himalayas? And in what country would you find the island of Rapa Nui?

items.title: Children had to use toilet in front of others in police watchhouse, tribunal told
items.description: Advocates for young people say conditions in a Queensland watch house have not improved since three teenagers' human rights were breached. A tribunal heard the boys had limited privacy and had to use the toilet in front of others.

items.title: The new political parties hoping to deceive 'useful idiots' in Victoria
items.description: New political parties are seeking to exploit Victoria's anachronistic electoral system in the upper house to harvest voters' preferences and funnel them wherever they please.

items.title: Why 10 years later stadiums are still a major bugbear of the AFLW
items.description: The AFL has introduced four double-headers this season, meaning games will be played at bigger venues, while the league remains steadfast on boutique grounds for standalone matches.

items.title: What Australia's economy could look like under One Nation

items.title: Man denied assisted dying wins partial victory in early test of ACT law
items.description: A tribunal has ruled on a man's bid to overturn his rejection from the ACT's assisted dying scheme in one of the first tests of how people can challenge such decisions.

items.title: Death of man experiencing homelessness in rural town prompts call for help
items.description: Millicent residents say they are concerned for the welfare of dozens of people sleeping rough in town.

items.title: Former ACT politician to stand trial on grooming charges
items.description: Former ACT Attorney-General Gordon Ramsay is committed to stand trial for allegedly grooming a teenage boy between 2022 and 2025.

items.title: Comm Games 'might look a little different' for swim star after broken back
items.description: Mollie O'Callaghan reveals she has defied doctors' diagnoses to swim at the Commonwealth Games and Pan Pacific Championships despite spinal fractures and a shoulder injury.
